questions.q:
Which of the following statements about molecular clouds are correct?
1. They consist mostly of molecular hydrogen.
2. They are among the coldest parts of the interstellar medium, which allows molecules to survive in them.
3. They appear opaque because of the dust grains within them.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are correct. Molecular clouds are cold, dense interstellar regions dominated by hydrogen molecules, and the low temperature together with shielding by dust lets molecules form and persist instead of being broken apart by radiation. The dust blocks background starlight, hence the name 'dark clouds', and the clouds have irregular shapes without sharp edges. They are stellar nurseries, and the Sun is thought to have formed in one; mapping their magnetic skeleton helps explain star formation.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 82; low temperature of molecular clouds is static

questions.q:
With reference to the nationwide HPV vaccination drive that began on 28 February 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Vaccination is voluntary and needs parental consent.
2. It follows a two-dose schedule spaced six months apart.
3. Girls already vaccinated with Cervavac are included to boost their immunity.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The drive is voluntary, free and conditional on parental consent. Statement 2 is wrong because it uses a single intramuscular dose of Gardasil-4, which simplifies delivery after a 90-day intensive phase. Statement 3 is wrong because those who have received any HPV vaccine are excluded, as are girls who are pregnant or allergic, and those outside age 14. Stressing cancer prevention is meant to counter the stigma of a sexually transmitted infection.

questions.q:
With regard to the digital backbone of India's immunisation programme, consider the following statements:
1. U-WIN is the platform that tracks cold-chain stock of vaccines at storage points.
2. eVIN is the platform on which each vaccine beneficiary registers and receives a digital certificate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct, as the roles are swapped. U-WIN handles beneficiary registration and vaccination records. The Electronic Vaccine Intelligence Network, eVIN, tracks stock and supply. The HPV drive relies on both as its digital backbone, one to follow the girl and the other to follow the vaccine. Together they support a campaign restricted to designated government facilities, where data on coverage and availability helps in reaching the target of about 1.15 crore girls and in following up with those left out.

questions.q:
Governance of dual-use technologies relies on different kinds of mechanisms. Match List-I (Mechanism) with List-II (Example):
List-I
A. Preventing malicious development
B. Controlling access
C. Monitoring and compliance
List-II
1. Inspection and verification under IAEA safeguards
2. Treaties banning weaponisation, such as the Biological and Chemical Weapons Conventions
3. Export controls, licensing and limits on technology transfer
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Treaties such as the Biological and Chemical Weapons Conventions aim to stop weaponisation at source, so they prevent malicious development. Export controls, licensing and limits on technology transfer, applied through regimes such as Wassenaar and the Australia Group, control who gets sensitive items. IAEA safeguards inspect and verify that nuclear material stays in peaceful use, which is monitoring and compliance. The analysis argues that all three tools lag behind AI, synthetic biology and DNA synthesis, where 'sequences of concern' remain loosely defined.

questions.q: MASLD, mentioned in the World Obesity Atlas 2026 estimates for Indian children, refers to
o: a malabsorption syndrome linked to micronutrient deficiency
fatty liver disease associated with metabolic dysfunction
a genetic disorder of muscle wasting among adolescents
a form of hypertension that begins in childhood
questions.e: MASLD stands for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the current term for fat build-up in the liver related to obesity and insulin resistance. The Atlas estimated several million Indian children to be affected in 2025 because of high BMI. It is neither a muscle disorder nor a deficiency syndrome, and although hypertension is listed separately as a result of high BMI, it is not the same as MASLD. Together, these support the argument that India faces a double burden of malnutrition.

questions.q:
Scientists at CERN recently moved antiprotons by road. Consider the following statements:
1. An antiproton is much lighter than a proton but carries the same positive charge.
2. The antiproton was first identified by Paul Dirac and Carl Anderson.
3. The observed dominance of matter over antimatter remains a puzzle, as the Big Bang should have produced both in equal amounts.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct, and it explains why antimatter research matters. Statement 1 is wrong: an antiproton has the same mass and spin as a proton, with negative charge. Statement 2 is wrong: Emilio Segre and Owen Chamberlain identified it and won the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics; Dirac predicted antimatter theoretically, and Anderson discovered the positron. Moving antiprotons is hard because antimatter annihilates on contact with ordinary matter, so special confinement is needed.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 81; Dirac and Anderson are static

questions.q: The Union Budget 2026-27 offered a 'safe harbour of 15 per cent on cost' relating to data centres. In tax policy, a safe harbour means
o: an exemption from all corporate income tax for the data centre company
a physically secured zone in which foreign data cannot be accessed by Indian authorities
an insurance fund that compensates data centres for losses from cyber-attacks
a pre-agreed margin which tax authorities accept for related-party transactions, cutting down transfer-pricing disputes
questions.e: A safe harbour sets a margin, here 15 per cent over cost, that authorities will accept where an Indian data centre serves a related foreign company, so disputes over transfer pricing are reduced. It does not abolish tax on the Indian entity; the separate tax holiday to 2047 is for eligible foreign cloud companies. It has nothing to do with cyber insurance or with legal immunity from access to data. The measure seeks tax certainty to draw investment into capacity.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 69-70; transfer-pricing meaning is static

questions.q:
Among the following food items:
1. Salt
2. Milk
3. Edible oil
4. Wheat flour
5. Sugar
How many of the above are among the staples for which FSSAI has laid down fortification standards?
questions.e: The first four are covered; the fifth is not. FSSAI's standards under the Fortification of Foods Regulations, 2018 apply to five staples: rice, wheat flour, edible oil, milk and salt. Sugar is not among them, and it is an unlikely vehicle given concerns over excess intake. The regulator chose foods consumed widely and regularly so that a small addition can reach many people. Critics, however, stress lower bioavailability and the risks of excess intake, and urge diet diversification including millets.

questions.q:
Statement-I: NavIC's Standard Positioning Service signals are not interoperable with GPS or Galileo.
Statement-II: Many smartphones and navigation devices do not support NavIC.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is wrong: NavIC's civil signals are interoperable with GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou. Statement-II is correct and is a separate practical weakness, as chipset support remains limited. Other concerns include an absence of a dedicated management body such as the US GPS Directorate or the EU's EUSPA for Galileo, ISRO serving as both designer and operator, and a launch rate slower than satellite decay. These matter because the system is meant to provide sovereign navigation after the Kargil experience.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The siting of large data centres in Chennai and Bengaluru raises particular sustainability concerns.
Statement-II: Cooling a hyperscale facility can require water running into millions of litres a day, and these cities have faced water stress.
Statement-III: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in 2023.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: All statements are correct, but only Statement-II explains the first. A 100 MW facility can use up to 2 million litres of water a day, which is risky for cities that have already seen shortages. The data protection law is an accurate fact that supports data demand, but it does not account for the environmental worry. More than 70 per cent of capacity sits in four metros, which is why resource-first siting based on grid, groundwater and climate hazard is recommended.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Trying to smother a burning lithium-ion battery pack by cutting off air often fails to stop the fire.
Statement-II: Cells in thermal runaway can release oxygen internally and so sustain combustion by themselves.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. Decomposing cell materials supply oxygen from within, so the reaction continues without outside air. Fires therefore burn hotter and need large volumes of water for sustained cooling, along with special suppression methods. The chain reaction moves from cell to cell through tightly packed packs and can vent toxic gases such as hydrogen fluoride. The Indore incident also showed external factors at work, such as LPG cylinders nearby and electronic locks failing during an outage.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Type of fortification) with List-II (Example):
List-I
A. Bio-fortification
B. Industrial fortification
C. Home fortification
List-II
1. Iodine added to salt during processing
2. Nutrient-powder sachets added at the time of eating
3. Vitamin A-rich orange sweet potato
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Bio-fortification raises nutrients while the crop grows, by breeding or genetic modification, as with orange sweet potato. Industrial fortification adds nutrients at processing, as with salt iodisation or mixing fortified kernels into rice. Home fortification happens at the point of use through sprinkles or sachets. The distinction matters for policy: the method used under PMGKAY was industrial, and its nutrient stability under storage was what an IIT Kharagpur study questioned before the pause.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Kavach, whose extension across railway zones was approved in March 2026, is NOT correct?
o: It repeats line-side signals inside the cab, which helps during fog.
It was licensed from the European Train Control System and adapted for Indian track gauges.
It is designed to prevent Signal Passing at Danger.
It can apply the brakes automatically if a loco pilot fails to act.
questions.e: Kavach is an indigenous system developed through the Research Designs and Standards Organisation, so the claim of European licensing is false. The rest is accurate. It acts as both automatic train protection and collision avoidance, applying brakes if trains are on a collision course, through head-on, rear-end or side-on conflicts. It stops a train from passing a red signal, repeats signals in the cab for low-visibility conditions, and can send emergency messages along with automatic horn operation.

questions.q: V2X technology, for which the Union Government reportedly began spectrum allocation, is best described as one that
o: replaces fuel-based vehicles with hydrogen-based ones on selected corridors
uses cameras inside a vehicle to monitor driver fatigue and alert the driver
converts electric vehicles into mobile power banks that feed electricity into the grid
allows vehicles to exchange data with each other, with pedestrians and cyclists, and with roadside infrastructure
questions.e: V2X means vehicle-to-everything, and includes vehicle-to-vehicle, vehicle-to-pedestrian and vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. Its road safety value is that a car can 'see' vulnerable users or hazards beyond line of sight, while traffic flows can also be improved. It needs dedicated radio spectrum, hence the news. Feeding power back to the grid is a separate idea, vehicle-to-grid. In-cabin fatigue cameras are onboard assistance, not communication with others, and hydrogen fuel has no bearing here.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 79; vehicle-to-grid distinction is static

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about dimethyl ether (DME), for which CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory has developed a process technology, are correct?
1. Like diethyl ether, it readily forms explosive peroxides when exposed to air for long periods.
2. It liquefies under pressure.
3. It has uses as an aerosol propellant and a refrigerant.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The gas liquefies under modest pressure, which makes it easy to handle with LPG-type systems, and it has uses as a fuel, propellant, solvent and refrigerant. Statement 1 is wrong: DME, unlike diethyl ether, does not form peroxides on long exposure to air, which is one of its advertised safety properties. It burns cleanly with little soot or sulphur oxide, and that makes it attractive as an LPG partial substitute that can be made from Indian coal, methanol or captured carbon dioxide.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 82; diethyl ether comparison is static

questions.q:
The Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets seeks an integrated value chain. Arrange the following stages in the correct order of production:
1. Alloys
2. Rare earth oxides
3. Finished magnets
4. Metals
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The chain runs from rare earth oxides to metals, then alloys, and finally finished magnets. The scheme insists on this integrated structure because mere assembly of imported alloy would leave India exposed at the concentrated upstream refining steps. Five beneficiaries are to be chosen by global bidding under the Ministry of Heavy Industries. The design thus reflects a concern with supply-chain resilience, since processing rather than mining is often the main global chokepoint in this sector.

questions.q:
In the context of India's research funding, consider the following statements:
1. The Anusandhan National Research Foundation was established by an Act of Parliament.
2. A Parliamentary Standing Committee reviewing the IndiaAI Mission asked for the real impact of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and the Research Development and Innovation Fund to be assessed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Foundation was created by a 2023 Act, as the apex body for funding research. The committee's concern was that AI research funding concentrates in IITs and national labs, and it wanted a broader evaluation of these two instruments so that research could be democratised. The same review flagged low absorption of funds, costly hardware and environmental worries over sovereign data centres, and recommended consultation with stakeholders and environmental experts.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 76-77; ANRF Act, 2023 is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to fat tissue:
Feature : Type of fat
1. Releases leptin, which reduces appetite : White fat
2. Chief store of energy as triglycerides : Brown fat
3. Activated on cold exposure to generate heat : Brown fat
4. Releases adiponectin, which helps regulate insulin and blood sugar : Brown fat
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. White fat, the most abundant fat in adults, stores energy as triglycerides and also acts as an endocrine organ, releasing both leptin and adiponectin, so pairs 2 and 4 wrongly credit its roles to brown fat. Brown fat, found mainly in the neck and upper chest, burns energy to give off heat when the brain signals cold exposure. That calorie-dissipating ability is why researchers see it as a promising target for weight-loss treatments.

questions.q: V.O. Chidambaranar Port became the first Indian port to launch a Digital Twin initiative. Which one of the following correctly describes the idea and the setting?
o: It is a static three-dimensional design model of a riverine port in Kerala, used only at the planning stage.
It is a second physical harbour built as a backup to a major port.
It is a cargo-tracking mobile application for a minor port on Gujarat's coast.
It is a live virtual replica of the assets of a major port, built as an artificial deep-sea harbour at Thoothukudi.
questions.e: A digital twin is a virtual replica fed by live data from sensors, GPS, LiDAR, drones and cameras, which allows monitoring, simulation and predictive analytics through an asset's lifecycle. It is more than a static design model or simple cargo tracking. The port, formerly Tuticorin, is an artificial deep-sea harbour at Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu, not a riverine or Kerala port, and it is a major port. It has long been linked with maritime trade and pearl fisheries.

questions.q:
With reference to rare earth permanent magnets, consider the following statements:
1. Neodymium, used in Nd-Fe-B magnets, is a rare earth element.
2. The rare earth group consists of 17 elements, namely the lanthanides along with scandium and yttrium.
3. Iron and boron, the other main ingredients in these magnets, are also classified as rare earth elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Neodymium is a lanthanide, and scandium and yttrium are included because of their chemical similarity. Statement 3 is wrong: iron and boron are common elements outside this group, and the magnet draws its strength from the neodymium. Rare earths are also different from the broader official list of critical minerals. Strong magnets of this kind are central to electric vehicles, wind power, electronics and defence, hence the supply-chain concern behind India's new scheme.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 79-80; rare-earth composition is static

questions.q: The '90-70-90' targets of the WHO Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative, to be met by 2030, refer respectively to
o: 90 per cent of women screened by age 35, 70 per cent of girls vaccinated by age 15 and 90 per cent of cases cured
90 countries adopting vaccination, 70 countries adopting screening and 90 per cent of health budgets ring-fenced
90 per cent reduction in mortality, 70 per cent reduction in incidence and 90 per cent coverage of boys
90 per cent of girls fully vaccinated by age 15, 70 per cent of women screened by ages 35 and 45, and 90 per cent of those with disease treated or managed
questions.e: The three pillars are prevention, screening and treatment. Ninety per cent of girls are to be vaccinated by 15, 70 per cent of women screened with a high-performance test by 35 and again by 45, and 90 per cent of those with pre-cancer treated and those with invasive cancer managed. The other versions shuffle these or invent mortality and budget measures. India's drive for 14-year-olds supports the first pillar, while screening and treatment still depend on general health capacity.

questions.q:
Consider the following satellites:
1. IRNSS-1B
2. IRNSS-1F
3. IRNSS-1I
4. NVS-02
How many of the above could provide position, navigation and timing services after the March 2026 clock failure?
questions.e: IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I could, and the third working spacecraft was NVS-01. IRNSS-1F dropped out when its last atomic clock stopped, which triggered the news. NVS-02 never reached its designated orbit after its 2025 launch on GSLV-F15, and it cannot serve this function. Since at least four satellites with working clocks are needed for proper operation, three left the service short. Six of the eleven satellites meant for NavIC have failed because of clock problems, which raises questions about replenishment.

questions.q:
With reference to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which is supplying doses for India's HPV campaign, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations created in 1948.
2. Its work in India includes reducing the number of 'zero-dose' children.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Zero-dose children are those who have missed even the first routine vaccines, and Gavi's work in India seeks to reduce their number while integrating HPV and typhoid conjugate vaccines into routine immunisation. Statement 1 is wrong: Gavi is a public-private partnership formed in 2000, joining developing countries, donors, WHO, UNICEF, the World Bank, vaccine makers and the Gates Foundation; 1948 is WHO's founding year. India's 2023 partnership with Gavi was worth US$ 250 million.

questions.q:
On India's data centre ecosystem, consider the following statements:
1. An RBI directive requires payment-system data to be stored in India.
2. Direct-to-chip and immersion cooling are approaches being suggested for data centres to manage heat from dense computing loads.
3. The GI Cloud initiative 'MeghRaj' is run by the Ministry of Power.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The RBI's rule on payment data is a key demand driver for domestic capacity, along with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Advanced cooling draws heat more directly from the hardware, which can lower water and energy use for AI workloads. Statement 3 is wrong: MeghRaj is an e-governance cloud delivered through the National Informatics Centre, under the electronics ministry, and has nothing to do with the Ministry of Power.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Xi-cc-plus has about four times the mass of a proton even though both contain three quarks.
Statement-II: Charm quarks are far heavier than up quarks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. A proton has two up quarks and one down quark, while Xi-cc-plus has two charm quarks in place of the up quarks. Since charm quarks are far heavier, the mass rises a great deal without any change in quark number. Studying such particles helps physicists understand how the strong force binds composite particles. The discovery was the Large Hadron Collider's 80th new particle, alongside earlier landmarks such as the Higgs boson.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 72-73; quark mass comparison is static

questions.q:
Among the four fundamental forces, consider the following statements about the strong force, which the discovery of Xi-cc-plus helps to study:
1. It weakens the bond between quarks as they come closer, and is far weaker than electromagnetism.
2. It operates over extremely short distances, much smaller than the diameter of an atom.
3. It binds quarks together into composite particles such as protons and neutrons.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The strong force holds quarks inside protons, neutrons and other hadrons, and its reach is a tiny fraction of atomic size. Statement 1 fails on the main claim, because the strong force is about a hundred times stronger than electromagnetism at those distances, which is why nuclei hold together despite repulsion among protons. Studying heavy-quark baryons offers a cleaner test of its behaviour, a reason doubly charmed particles interest physicists.

questions.q: In the context of electronic warfare, what is the difference between GPS jamming and GPS spoofing?
o: Jamming affects only military receivers, whereas spoofing affects only civilian receivers.
Jamming requires destroying a satellite, whereas spoofing requires hacking its ground control.
Jamming drowns out the genuine signal, whereas spoofing feeds the receiver false signals so that it computes a wrong position.
Jamming alters a satellite's orbit, whereas spoofing alters its onboard clock.
questions.e: Jamming is denial: strong noise on the same frequency prevents a receiver from locking on to genuine signals. Spoofing is deception: counterfeit signals make the receiver accept a wrong position or time, which can be more dangerous because the user may not notice. Neither needs physical attack on a satellite, nor do they alter its orbit or clock, and civil and military receivers can both be vulnerable. Such non-kinetic methods are cited as leading examples of civilian technology being turned to war.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 82-85; technical distinction is static

questions.q:
With respect to science and technology initiatives in the news, how many of the following pairs of initiative and responsible body are correctly matched?
Initiative : Body
1. GARBH-INi pregnancy cohort study : Department of Biotechnology
2. Scheme to promote sintered rare earth permanent magnets : Ministry of Mines
3. Dimethyl ether production process technology : CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory
4. IndiaAI Mission : Department of Science and Technology
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. GARBH-INi is a flagship programme of the Department of Biotechnology, and CSIR-NCL at Pune developed the DME process as an LPG substitute. Pair 2 is wrong: the magnet scheme, worth Rs 7,280 crore, was put out to bid by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, even though rare earths sound like a mining subject. Pair 4 is wrong: the IndiaAI Mission is implemented by MeitY, which is why the parliamentary committee directed its funding concerns to that ministry.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 76-77, 79-80, 82; CSIR-NCL location is static

questions.q:
With reference to the regulator that barred advertising of GLP-1 drugs in March 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
2. It is headed by the Drugs Controller General of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The organisation is the national drug regulator and functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not the Department of Pharmaceuticals, which handles industry promotion, pricing support and Jan Aushadhi. The Drugs Controller General heads it and approves new drugs and clinical trials. Candidates often confuse the two because both concern medicines. GLP-1 receptor agonists, first made for type 2 diabetes and now widely used for weight loss, prompted the advertising ban because of misuse.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 80-81; CDSCO's ministry and head are static

questions.q:
In the context of the particles discovered at the Large Hadron Collider, consider the following statements:
1. Protons and neutrons are baryons.
2. Toponium, reported at the Large Hadron Collider, consists of a top quark bound to its antiquark.
3. Pions and kaons are baryons.
4. Xi-cc-plus differs from the doubly charmed particle reported in 2017 in having a down quark in place of an up quark.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Baryons have three quarks, as in protons and neutrons. Toponium is the most massive composite particle yet observed. Both charmed baryons have two charm quarks, while the third quark is down for Xi-cc-plus and up for the 2017 particle. Statement 3 is wrong because pions and kaons are mesons, made of a quark and an antiquark. Baryons and mesons together form hadrons, and all depend on the strong force for binding.

questions.q:
In the context of technology terms in the news, consider the following pairs:
Term : Field in which it is used
1. Thermal propagation test : Safety certification of electric-vehicle battery packs
2. Signal Passing at Danger : Railway train protection
3. Phase-change cooling : Managing heat in battery packs
4. Sequences of concern : Detection of spoofed satellite navigation signals
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. AIS-156 requires thermal propagation testing so that occupants get at least five minutes to escape a battery fire. Kavach is designed to stop trains from passing a red signal, the event called Signal Passing at Danger. Phase-change cooling uses an evaporating coolant to absorb more heat in packs. Pair 4 is wrong: 'sequences of concern' is a biosecurity term for dangerous DNA sequences that synthesis providers should screen, not a navigation-spoofing concept.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 79-85; Vision IAS p. 79

questions.q:
Regarding safety measures for lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, consider the following statements:
1. AIS-156 is a Bureau of Energy Efficiency label that rates batteries by charging speed.
2. Solid-state batteries raise leakage risk because they use more liquid electrolyte than conventional cells.
3. A Battery Management System is a physical firewall placed between cells to stop flames.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. AIS-156 is an automotive safety standard associated with the Automotive Research Association of India, and it mandates thermal propagation testing and at least five minutes for occupants to escape, so it is not an efficiency label. Solid-state cells use solid electrolytes, which cut leakage and runaway risk. A Battery Management System is an electronic control that regulates temperature, voltage and charging. Physical firewalls are a separate containment measure, with insulation and compartments used to slow any spread.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Over fifty countries vaccinate boys as well as girls against HPV.
Statement-II: HPV infection is linked to cancers in men, such as penile, anal and oropharyngeal cancers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. Countries like the US, Canada and Germany use gender-neutral programmes because boys benefit directly and also reduce transmission. HPV is not a women-only risk: many men carry a genital type, and some develop cancer. India's first phase covers only 14-year-old girls, prioritising cervical cancer, a leading cancer among Indian women. Exclusion of boys is listed among concerns, and it could be a future area of expansion subject to cost and supply.

questions.q: Which one of the following is true of Gardasil-4, the vaccine used in India's HPV drive?
o: Types 6 and 11 in it mainly cause genital warts, and types 16 and 18 are the main high-risk cancer-causing types.
Types 6 and 11 in it are the main causes of cervical cancer, and types 16 and 18 cause warts.
It is a live attenuated vaccine produced by the Serum Institute of India.
It covers nine HPV types, including all of the types known to cause cancer.
questions.e: The vaccine covers four types. Types 16 and 18 cause about 70 per cent of cervical cancers globally and over 80 per cent in India, whereas types 6 and 11 mainly cause warts. The second description reverses this. A nine-type vaccine is a different product, Gardasil-9, and in any case at least 14 types can cause cancer. It is not live attenuated, and Serum Institute makes Cervavac, the indigenous counterpart, while Gardasil doses for the campaign are supplied through Gavi.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 75-76; vaccine platform and wart types are static

questions.q:
With reference to India's NavIC system, consider the following statements:
1. Its first-generation constellation places satellites in both geostationary and inclined geosynchronous orbits.
2. First-generation satellites offer the Standard Positioning Service on the L5 and S bands.
3. The NVS series adds the L1 band.
4. NVS-01 was the first of these satellites to carry an indigenous atomic clock.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Three geostationary and four inclined geosynchronous slots give regional coverage up to about 1,500 km beyond India. The L5 and S bands limited adoption because mainstream phones favour L1, so second-generation NVS satellites added L1 to improve device compatibility. The earlier spacecraft used imported rubidium clocks that failed repeatedly, as on IRNSS-1F, so NVS-01, launched in 2023 by GSLV-F12, was significant for its domestically made clock.
